shared_elements: quadruped creature in profile with legs indicated
frontal anthropomorphic/standing figure in higher relief with limbs (A) alongside profile creatures
elements arranged in horizontal registers/bands on a flat upright slab
band of repeated geometric pattern (chevron/zigzag/herringbone) in B and repeated linear incisions in A
combination of several distinct creatures on one surface without a narrative ground line
justification: Both surfaces show flat upright slabs carved with a mix of profile animals rendered in shallow, flat-topped relief combined with a more strongly modelled anthropomorphic/standing form, and both organise their motifs into stacked horizontal zones separated by patterned or linear bands, which is a fairly specific shared scheme. The main difference in content is that B presents a rich inventory of identifiable creatures (a row of birds, a snake, a fox-like animal, a large standing bird) in several registers, whereas A centres on a single frontal figure with arms and legs flanked by only a couple of indistinct animals, and none of the specific creature-to-creature relationships in B recur in A.
